fields.claim_quote: The above implies that both intervals contain the same primes. We also point out that the upper bound of the larger interval, $\left\lfloor P_k+2\sqrt{P_k}\right\rfloor+1$, cannot be a prime since it is an even number for any $k$.
fields.explanation: The source asserts parity for every prime index, not eventually. At the original prime3, Mathlib Real.sqrt and Int.floor give7, which is odd and prime. The certificate no longer substitutes a square-bound checker for the floor expression.
fields.flaw: For every prime P_k, floor(P_k+2√P_k)+1 is even and therefore cannot be prime.
fields.problem: Title: On primes amongst squares of naturals
fields.witness: Take P_k=3, which is prime. Since 3<2√3<4, floor(3+2√3)+1=6+1=7. Thus the claimed value is odd and is itself prime, directly refuting the claim.
